Question B-007-007-002.

Why the correct answer is right: Slight bending in the troposphere extends the radio horizon for very high frequency (VHF) signals such as two metres. That lets stations communicate somewhat farther than a simple straight-line path would allow.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "It causes them to travel shorter distances": Tropospheric bending curves some energy with Earth instead of away from it, so the range tends to increase.
- sourceIndex 2: "It distorts the signal": Distortion can occur on some unusual paths, but ordinary tropospheric bending is mainly a range-extension effect.
- sourceIndex 3: "It interferes with short-range communications": The effect is not defined as interference. It is refraction that can help beyond-normal contacts.
